item.title: HURIWA urges Otti to pay 4,700 teachers
item.description: …Raises concerns over unpaid allowances, rural teachers’ welfare By Chioma Obinna The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has called on Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, to pay 4,700 newly recruited primary school teachers allegedly working without salaries. The association described the reported delay as unfair to the teachers, who it said were recruited and deployed to public schools, particularly in rural communities, but had yet to receive their first salaries since resuming duties last month. In a statement on Tuesday, HURIWA’s National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, criticised reports that the teachers might not be paid until January 2027 because of a three-month probationary period. “Governor Otti must explain why 4,700 teachers employed by his government should work for months without salaries. These are not volunteering or charity workers. They are employees who deserve to be paid for their services. Probation must not become a licence for exploitation,” the group said. HURIWA also alleged that the teachers’ training allowances had remained unpaid since September, questioning how they were expected to cover transportation costs and meet their family responsibilities without income. The association further asked the state government to explain why the newly recruited teachers were allegedly excluded from the N1 billion reportedly released for teachers during the 2026 World Teachers’ Day celebration. It said the affected teachers claimed that existing teachers received N50,000 each from the fund, while the new recruits were left out. Beyond the alleged non-payment of salaries and allowances, HURIWA raised concerns about the welfare of teachers posted to rural communities, citing inadequate transportation and accommodation, as well as poor school infrastructure. It urged the state government to deploy some of the electric buses reportedly procured by the administration to transport teachers to rural schools, provide affordable accommodation and teachers’ quarters, and rehabilitate dilapidated classrooms. “Governor Otti cannot claim to be transforming Abia’s education sector while the teachers recruited to drive that transformation allegedly beg for transportation money and wait for months to receive their salaries,” the association said. HURIWA demanded the immediate payment of outstanding salaries and allowances, an investigation into the alleged exclusion of the new recruits from the Teachers’ Day payment, and improved welfare and working conditions. “These 4,700 teachers are not volunteers. They are not charity workers. They are employees recruited by the Abia State Government and deployed to serve the state. Governor Otti must pay them, protect their dignity and provide the conditions they need to teach. Government cannot demand their labour and deny them their wages,” it said. item.title: Pochettino open to Man United talks as Carrick’s future hangs in balance
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Mauricio Pochettino would be open to discussing the Manchester United head coach’s position if the club approaches him, as Michael Carrick faces growing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford. Sky Sports News reports that no final decision has been made on Carrick, while Pochettino is open to talks and could cost United about £7 million to release from his United States contract. United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are due to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe on Wednesday to review the season and discuss their recommendations on Carrick. The club is also assessing possible alternatives. Carrick’s position has come under pressure after United went eight consecutive Premier League matches without a win. The team’s late fightbacks in recent matches have offered some encouragement, but have not eased doubts about its overall form. Pochettino, who previously managed Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain, recently extended his contract as US head coach through 2030. United have considered him for the Old Trafford job before, but there have been no substantive talks with potential replacements so far. United are expected to use the international break to assess the season before deciding their next step. Carrick remains in charge for now, with the club’s leadership weighing whether a change of coach would address the team’s struggles. item.title: ADC faults INEC for condemning ‘rig and die’, ignoring APC chairman’s AK-47 threat
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of applying double standards in tackling electoral violence, questioning its silence over an alleged AK-47 threat by an APC chairman against opposition voters. The party said INEC’s condemnation of the ‘rig and die’ slogan ahead of the 2027 general elections was appropriate, but insisted that the commission must show equal urgency when threats emanate from the ruling party. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC recalled remarks attributed to Edo State APC Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, threatening to use AK-47 rifles against those who refused to vote for President Bola Tinubu. “Why has INEC found its voice to condemn ‘rig and die’ but remained conspicuously silent on the threat by an APC chairman to use AK-47 rifles against opposition voters? Is a slogan more dangerous than a gun?” the party asked. It also challenged INEC to disclose whether it had referred the alleged threat to security agencies. “If INEC is concerned about the language of those warning against electoral rigging, should it not be even more concerned when a political party official threatens voters with AK-47 rifles? Has INEC referred the matter to security agencies? If not, why not?” the ADC queried. The opposition party maintained that it rejected electoral violence regardless of the political affiliation of those making the threats. “However, INEC cannot demand peaceful elections without demonstrating equal concern for those threatened with violence. Its responsibility is not merely to condemn inflammatory language, but to demand an environment that permits every Nigerian to vote freely,” Abdullahi said. item.title: Police arrest two over N1.35m robbery in Kano
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has arrested two suspected armed robbers over the theft of N1.35 million and other valuables at Falgore Forest in Doguwa Local Government Area of the state. The suspects, identified as Sulaiman Alhaji Umaru, 35, from Kaduna State, and Abubakar Sale, 22, from Gwarzo Local Government Area of Kano State, were arrested on November 6 at Dogon Dutse, Falgore Forest. The Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Tuesday, saying operatives of the Doguwa Division made the arrests following credible intelligence. According to Kiyawa, one of the suspects, Umaru, confessed to conspiring with seven others to rob Adamu Sa’adu of N1.35 million and other valuables in the Falgore Forest area. He said the police recovered N600,000, nine mobile phones, knives and sticks from the suspects. The command said efforts were ongoing to apprehend the remaining suspects, while investigation into the robbery continued. The Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the officers for the operation and urged residents to continue providing credible information to support efforts to tackle crime. He assured residents of the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property across the state. The post Police arrest two over N1.35m robbery in Kano appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Army renames Calabar barracks after late COAS Attahiru
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Army has renamed Akim Barracks, Headquarters 13 Brigade, Calabar, Cross River State, after the late former Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Ibrahim Attahiru, in recognition of his service and sacrifice to the nation. The renaming ceremony was performed on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, by the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, during his operational visit to Cross River State. A statement by Army Headquarters said the honour recognised Attahiru’s exceptional service, exemplary leadership and ultimate sacrifice in defence of the country. Speaking at the ceremony, Shaibu described the renaming as a deliberate act of remembrance and an enduring affirmation of the institutional values that define the Nigerian Army. He said the late general exemplified courage, professional competence, discipline and selfless devotion to duty, particularly during a challenging period in the country’s security history when the Army faced complex and evolving threats. Although his tenure as COAS was brief, Shaibu said Attahiru’s commitment to operational effectiveness, personnel welfare, professionalism and the fighting spirit of troops continued to resonate within the Army. He noted that immortalising the late military chief, who once commanded the barracks, went beyond preserving his memory, as it established a lasting connection between the Army’s heritage and the responsibilities of present and future generations of military personnel. The COAS charged officers and soldiers of 13 Brigade to reflect the honour through exemplary leadership, discipline, integrity, operational excellence and stronger relationships with the communities they were deployed to protect. He further urged them to uphold the highest standards of military conduct and contribute to building a well-trained, adequately equipped and highly motivated force capable of discharging its constitutional responsibilities. Earlier, the General Officer Commanding 82 Division of the Nigerian Army and Commander of Joint Task Force South East, Operation Udoka, Major General Ayobami Fadairo, commended the COAS for his commitment to troop welfare and the decision to immortalise the late general. He said the gesture would strengthen institutional pride and boost the morale of personnel serving in the division. The Cross River State Governor, Senator Bassey Otu, represented by his deputy, Dr Peter Odey, also paid tribute to the late military chief, describing his life as an enduring example of exemplary leadership, humility and patriotism worthy of emulation, particularly by military personnel. In her remarks, the wife of the late general, Mrs Fatima Attahiru, thanked the COAS and the Nigerian Army for the honour, describing it as a lasting source of pride and comfort to the family. item.title: Lens sack coach after 9-1 defeat to Como in Champions League
item.description: Lens have sacked coach Yannick Cahuzac less than a week after their 9-1 Champions League defeat at home to Como, a source close to the French club told AFP on Tuesday, confirming a report from sports daily L’Equipe. Cahuzac, who was appointed by Lens less than two months ago, lost his job after the French Cup winners’ humiliating loss to Como last Wednesday, as well as a subsequent 2-1 reversal at their Stade Bollaert-Delelis home against Marseille on Sunday in Ligue 1. “We feel like we’re in a bad way. We feel that Wednesday’s result has left its mark,” Cahuzac admitted after the match against Marseille. “We’ve managed to pick ourselves up. But we’ve got quite a few gaps in the team, and we feel we’ve lost our confidence.” The former Lens captain took over from Dino Toppmoeller in mid-September following the German coach’s surprise departure after just four Ligue 1 matchdays. In nine matches in charge of Lens, Cahuzac has secured just three wins and suffered six defeats across all competitions as Lens lounge in 11th place domestically. Crucially, the 41-year-old has failed to pick up a single point in Europe, losing to Sporting Lisbon and Club Brugge, as well as the Como thrashing — the joint record for the biggest winning margin in the modern Champions League. “In front of our fans, here at Bollaert, this is unacceptable,” Lens chairman Joseph Oughourlian told Ligue 1+ on Sunday, adding that he had had the words “never again” painted on the walls of the changing room. Last season under current Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage, Lens won the French Cup and finished second in the league behind Paris Saint-Germain. item.title: 2027: Awkunanaw youths endorse Mbah, Tinubu
item.description: …Reject rival governorship bids, pledge support for APC candidates By Chinedu Adonu Youths from Awkunanaw in Enugu State have endorsed Governor Peter Mbah for a second term and President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, pledging to mobilise support for all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the state. The youths, under the aegis of the Awkunanaw Political Forum (APF), also rejected governorship ambitions by other Awkunanaw indigenes seeking to challenge Mbah, urging them to shelve their aspirations and support the incumbent governor. The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued on Tuesday following the group’s youth-led convention held at the Enugu South Local Government Secretariat on November 10, 2026. The communiqué, signed by the Director-General of APF, Hon. Nnamani Arinze Darlington, and the Executive Chairman of Enugu South Local Government, Hon. Caleb Onyema Ani, said the endorsement followed extensive consultations on the political and socio-economic development of the state. Declaring their support for Mbah, the group cited his administration’s investments in education, healthcare, roads, transportation and security. It specifically highlighted the establishment of 268 Smart Green Schools, 260 Type-2 Primary Healthcare Centres, construction of over 1,521 kilometres of roads, five transport terminals and the deployment of more than 100 compressed natural gas (CNG) buses. The forum also commended the governor for reviving moribund state-owned assets and completing abandoned projects, including Hotel Presidential, Nigergas Limited, Enugu United Palm Products Limited and the International Conference Centre. Describing Mbah as its preferred candidate, the group said his leadership and development agenda aligned with the collective aspirations of the people of Enugu State. Explaining its opposition to other Awkunanaw governorship bids, the forum recalled the support it said Nkanu East Local Government Area gave former Governor Chimaroke Nnamani during his tenure. “Our brothers from Nkanu East LGA showed us support during His Excellency, Dr Chimaroke Nnamani’s tenure. We can only return the favour by standing in solidarity behind the governor,” the communiqué stated. The youths also endorsed Tinubu for a second term, citing his administration’s economic reforms, Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) student loan scheme, consumer credit initiative, infrastructure projects and Presidential CNG Initiative. “We pledge our unalloyed loyalty to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and commit our organisational strength to ensuring total victory for him in 2027,” the communiqué stated. The forum further pledged to mobilise and campaign for APC candidates seeking legislative and executive positions across Enugu State. It urged Awkunanaw youths to remain united and actively participate in the political process, declaring: “One Voice. One Destiny. Awkunanaw for APC!” The post 2027: Awkunanaw youths endorse Mbah, Tinubu appeared first on Va

item.title: 2027: Jigawa is APC stronghold, Shettima claims
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse Vice President Kashim Shettima has claimed that Jigawa State is firmly behind the All Progressives Congress (APC), alleging that the four former governors of the state, including Sule Lamido, are supporting the ruling party. Shettima made the claim on Tuesday during the APC presidential campaign rally in Dutse, the state capital. He expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would secure massive votes in Jigawa in the 2027 presidential election, describing the state as an APC stronghold. According to him, prominent political figures in the state, including former governors Ali Sa’adu, Ibrahim Saminu Turaki, Muhammad Badaru Abubakar and Sule Lamido, are aligned with the APC. “Jigawa State is a home for the APC. All who and who, any politician who answers a name is with us. The former governors of Jigawa State, Ali Sa’adu, Ibrahim Saminu Turaki, Muhammad Badaru Abubakar, and even former Governor Alhaji Sule Lamido, are with us,” he said. Shettima, however, criticised the African Democratic Congress (ADC) vice-presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, over his comments accusing the late former President Muhammadu Buhari of deceiving him. The Vice President described Amaechi’s remarks as disrespectful to the North, saying Buhari remained one of the most respected political figures in the region. He said Northerners were known for their generosity and culture of appreciating and reciprocating acts of kindness. Shettima urged Jigawa residents to support Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections, saying it was time for the North to reciprocate what the President had done for the region and its people. He called on residents to turn out in large numbers to vote for Tinubu and all APC candidates, expressing confidence that the party would record a landslide victory in the state. item.title: Security of lives and property to top Tinubu’s agenda in 2nd term – APC
item.description: …No other Nigerian leader has radically transformed Nigerian than Tinubu-Alake boasts …Nigeria has been recording positive growth since Tinubu became President …Tinubu has given opportunity for 1.6 Nigerians to go to university-Idris By Soni Daniel (Northern Region Editor), Emma Ujah (Bureau Chief, Abuja) & Omeiza Ajayi President Bola Tinubu will pay priority attention to the protection of lives and property if he wins the forthcoming presidential election on January 16, 2027, the All Progressives Presidential Campaign Council revealed on Tuesday in Abuja. To achieve that objective, the party has promised to recruit 28,000 additional military personnel and 50,000 police officers, in order to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture. Beyond security, the APC administration under the leadership of President Tinubu plans to provide better quality and more affordable life for Nigerians; energy, infrastructure and economic growth, effective and accountable government. The Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr. Jumoke Oduwole, who is the Deputy Director, Directorate of Manifesto and Policy Development of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, made the declaration with the theme: “Transiting from Reforms to Shared Prosperity”. The party also promised to complete the establishment and equipping of the four new Army Divisions in Makurdi, Ilorin, Jalingo and Benin City; sustain intelligence-led kinetic operations against insurgents and kidnapping networks to degrade and dismantle their operating bases. In order to deal with kidnappers who have turned the nation’s forests into criminal hideouts, the ruling party promised to deploy trained Forest Guards, Agro-Rangers and Mining Marshals to safeguard agricultural belts, farming communities, grazing routes, national forest reserves and mineral deposits. The minister said the APC administration planned to make Nigeria a fortress where everyone would live happily to actualize their potentials without any form of fear. Femi Gbajabiamila, urged Nigerians to study the past and current manifestoes of the ruling All Progressives Congress and judge the party by the promises it has kept since 2023 when it assumed power. item.title: Troops rescue 21 kidnapped victims in Niger
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the 18 Brigade of the Nigerian Army have rescued 21 kidnapped victims following a gun battle with terrorists in Mariga Local Government Area of Niger State. The operation was conducted on Monday, November 9, 2026, after troops acted on intelligence about the activities of terrorists in Abaha and Sabon Wuri villages. The Brigade’s spokesman, Captain Adebayo Adewumi, said the troops deployed a fighting patrol to the area to intercept the criminal elements. He said a fierce gun battle ensued when the troops made contact with the terrorists, who were eventually overpowered and forced to flee into the nearby bush with suspected gunshot wounds. According to him, all 21 kidnapped victims were rescued unharmed and handed over to the appropriate authorities for reunification with their families after receiving first aid and undergoing preliminary profiling. Adewumi said troops had intensified operations through aggressive patrols and ambushes to track down and apprehend the fleeing terrorists. He urged residents of Mariga and neighbouring local government areas to promptly report anyone seen with gunshot wounds or any suspicious movement of criminal elements to the nearest security agency. The spokesman said the Commander of the 18 Brigade commended the troops for their gallantry, resilience and professionalism during the operation. He added that the commander had charged them to sustain the offensive and maintain operational momentum to rid the brigade’s area of responsibility of criminal activities and ensure the safety of law-abiding residents. Adewumi also attributed the operational gains to the recent expansion of the Nigerian Army and the additional operational capacity it had provided in the fight against kidnapping and terrorism in Niger State. item.title: UK, Nigeria deepen cooperation against financial crimes
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The United Kingdom and Nigeria have strengthened their strategic partnership to combat illicit financial flows, money laundering, fraud and terrorism financing through enhanced financial intelligence sharing and cross-border cooperation. The renewed cooperation followed high-level engagements in the UK involving Nigerian financial authorities, regulators and stakeholders from the banking and telecommunications sectors, according to a joint statement issued on Tuesday. The Nigerian delegation was led by the Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU), Hafsat Bakari, and included representatives of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) and Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC). A major highlight of the visit was an engagement with the UK’s Joint Money Laundering Intelligence Taskforce (JMLIT), a public-private partnership involving law enforcement agencies, regulators and private-sector institutions. The engagement provided an opportunity for both countries to exchange expertise on financial intelligence, information sharing and strategies for identifying and responding to illicit financial activities. The discussions also supported Nigeria’s plan to establish the Joint Financial Intelligence Cooperation (JFIC), a Nigerian-led initiative aimed at strengthening collaboration between government institutions and private-sector stakeholders. The initiative is expected to enhance the country’s capacity to detect and respond to money laundering, fraud, terrorism financing and other financial crimes through technology-driven cooperation and information sharing. During the visit, the delegation also met with representatives of the National Crime Agency (NCA), UK Financial Intelligence Unit (UKFIU), HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC), Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and HM Treasury. The discussions covered operational cooperation, trade-based money laundering, emerging financial threats, the UK’s Financial Action Task Force (FATF) presidency and opportunities for stronger international collaboration. Speaking on the partnership, Deputy Director, Illicit Finance and Anti-Corruption Department, FCDO, Chris Chalmers, said illicit financial flows harmed both countries’ economies and enabled the activities of transnational criminal networks. He said the engagements had helped consolidate cooperation on shared threats and global standards, including public-private partnerships. “The FCDO will continue to partner with Nigeria to operationalise the Joint Financial Intelligence Collaboration,” Chalmers said. Also speaking, Bakari said the increasingly interconnected and transnational nature of illicit financial networks made international cooperation essential. item.title: Fraud, weak investor protection threaten diaspora investments – NiDCOM
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NiDCOM) has identified fraudulent investment schemes, unverified investment channels and weak investor protection as major obstacles to attracting investments from Nigerians living abroad. The Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of NiDCOM, Abike Dabiri-Erewa, raised the concerns at the opening of the ninth Nigeria Diaspora Investment Summit 2026 in Abuja. She said the challenges had created a trust deficit that must be addressed to encourage more Nigerians in the diaspora to channel their resources into the domestic economy. The summit, organised in collaboration with the Nigeria Diaspora Summit Initiative, has the theme, “Bridging the Trust Gap: Connecting Diaspora Capital with Credible Home-based Opportunities.” Dabiri-Erewa described Nigerians living abroad as a significant economic force, saying their financial resources, expertise and global networks could contribute substantially to Nigeria’s ambition of building a $1tn economy. She, however, noted that concerns about transparency, fraudulent investment schemes and unreliable investment platforms continued to discourage potential investors. The NiDCOM chief called for effective regulatory safeguards, transparent investment processes and credible investment platforms to protect prospective investors and restore confidence. In his keynote address, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria, Shehu Usman Osidi, said the country must move beyond appealing to Nigerians abroad to invest and create an environment where they could independently verify, access and monitor investment opportunities from their locations. Osidi identified fraudulent property transactions, disputed land titles, abandoned projects, unfulfilled contractual obligations and mismanagement of investment funds as some of the factors undermining diaspora investors’ confidence. He called for stronger collaboration among government institutions, regulators and private-sector operators to promote transparency and safeguard diaspora investments. The FMBN chief executive said the Federal Government had taken steps to strengthen engagement with Nigerians abroad through the establishment of NiDCOM and the adoption of the National Diaspora Policy. He said the policy provided a framework for mobilising diaspora resources through investment, trade, entrepreneurship, public-private partnerships and knowledge transfer. Osidi also cited reforms under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, particularly those being pursued through the Presidential Enabling Business Environment Council, chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima. item.title: Join BRICS, Nigeria has no business with poverty — Falana tells FG
item.description: …Urges government to prioritise local refining, alternative economic policies By Favour Ulebor, Abuja A Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Femi Falana, has urged the Federal Government to join the BRICS economic bloc and adopt alternative economic policies, declaring that Nigeria has no business with poverty. Falana made the call while delivering the keynote address at the sixth edition of the Frontier Discourse Annual Public Lecture Series and Awards, organised by Pacesetter Frontier Magazine in Abuja on Tuesday. The human rights lawyer urged the government to reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imported petroleum products by strengthening domestic refining capacity and pursuing economic policies that promote local production and improve citizens’ welfare. He questioned why Nigeria, despite being a major crude oil-producing country, continued to rely on imported petroleum products to meet domestic consumption needs. Falana also called on the government to explore opportunities offered by BRICS, describing the economic bloc as an organisation established to challenge the dominance of the United States dollar and promote trade among member countries using their respective currencies. He argued that Nigeria needed to reconsider its dependence on economic policies promoted by the Bretton Woods institutions, including the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. He said, “Even within the bourgeois paradigm, within the bourgeois framework, consider some of them, including refining crude oil for domestic consumption in Nigeria. “No country in the world, none, has ever been developed by implementing the policies of these Bretton Woods institutions that were set up to underdevelop the economies of third world countries. “Join, join, join, not be a member country. Join the BRICS. I’m sure you know about the BRICS.” Explaining his position, Falana said the bloc offered opportunities for countries to challenge the dominance of the dollar and strengthen economic cooperation through local currency trade. “It’s an organisation set up to challenge the dominance of the dollar, to challenge the West, to mould the full-fledged members so that we can take advantage and trade among ourselves in your own currencies,” he said. The lawyer also said he had challenged what he described as the abandonment of the Nigeria-China currency swap arrangement. He further raised concerns over revenue losses associated with the suspension of cargo tracking, citing a Nigerian government report produced in 2021. According to him, the report showed that Nigeria lost $32bn during the 13 years in which cargo tracking was suspended, while another $10bn was lost between 2021 and 2025. He said the figures highlighted revenue leakages and untapped economic opportunities that the government needed to address. item.title: Senate summons aviation agencies over flight delays, safety risks
item.description: …Orders probe of prolonged aircraft holding during VIP movements By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has directed its Committee on Aviation to convene an urgent stakeholders’ meeting with relevant aviation authorities over prolonged aircraft holding in the air during Very Important Persons (VIPs) movements and other security-related operations at Nigerian airports. The Senate mandated the committee, chaired by Senator Abdulfatai Buhari (APC, Oyo North), to engage the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), Nigerian Airspace Management Agency (NAMA), Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) and Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) to address the disruptions and recommend measures to prevent their recurrence. The directive followed the adoption of an urgent motion sponsored by Senator Isah Jibrin (APC, Kogi East) during plenary on Tuesday, raising concerns over the safety implications of keeping commercial aircraft airborne for extended periods while awaiting clearance to land. The Senate amended the motion to include the NSIB among the agencies to be engaged and directed the committee to report back within two weeks. Jibrin, who moved the motion under Orders 41 and 51 of the Senate Standing Orders, drew attention to reported instances in which commercial aircraft scheduled to land at Nigerian airports were forced to remain in holding patterns for over an hour because landing operations had been temporarily suspended to accommodate VIP movements. He also noted that some international flights had been diverted to alternative airports within the country when access to their intended destinations was temporarily restricted. While acknowledging the legitimate security considerations surrounding VIP movements, the senator warned that such operations should not compromise aviation safety or unnecessarily disrupt commercial flight schedules. He expressed concern that prolonged airborne holding could increase fuel consumption, deplete operational reserves and expose aircraft to additional risks, including adverse weather conditions, air traffic congestion, diversion challenges and crew duty-time limitations. According to him, commercial aviation depends on coordinated schedules covering departure and arrival slots, fuel planning, crew duty hours, passenger connections, airport operations and air traffic management. He argued that where airport restrictions arising from VIP movements or other security operations were foreseeable, relevant authorities should coordinate ground delays, revised departure slots and flight sequencing rather than allow aircraft to take off and subsequently remain airborne awaiting clearance. The senator further maintained that information about anticipated airport restrictions should guide decisions on departure clearance and the management of arriving aircraft. item.title: FG expands health insurance coverage to 24m Nigerians
item.description: …Revitalises 3,526 PHCs, records over 20% drop in maternal deaths …Tinubu administration fulfils 41 health sector commitments — Pate By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has expanded health insurance coverage from 16 million to 24 million Nigerians, revitalised 3,526 primary healthcare centres (PHCs) and recorded a reduction of more than 20 per cent in maternal deaths arising from obstetric emergencies in government-supported facilities over the past three years. The government also said the President Bola Tinubu administration had fulfilled all 41 performance commitments set for the health sector at the beginning of his tenure. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja at the third Nigeria Health Sector-Wide Joint Annual Review (JAR), themed, “Make the Data Count”. Pate attributed the achievements to reforms under the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and the Health Sector Strategic Blueprint, which focus on strengthening healthcare governance, improving population health, expanding health financing, promoting local production of medical supplies and enhancing health security. According to him, the progress reflects the collective efforts of federal and state governments, development partners and other stakeholders. He said, “At the beginning of this administration, Mr President set performance commitments for the health sector. I am pleased to report that we have achieved all 41 commitments. These results reflect work across the federation and the institutions represented here today.” The minister disclosed that, for the third consecutive year, all states and more than 8,000 facilities supported by the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) had prepared plans for the coming year, aligned with budget priorities. He said cumulative BHCPF releases since 2019 had reached approximately ₦422.3bn as of October 2026, with ₦323.6bn disbursed to the fund’s gateways, including ₦249.5bn under the Tinubu administration. Pate added that the government had signed a memorandum of understanding with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) to strengthen the tracking of the funds and promote accountability. On health insurance, he said coverage had increased from approximately 16 million to 24 million Nigerians within three years, representing eight million additional enrollees. On primary healthcare delivery, the minister said 3,526 centres had been revitalised in collaboration with state governments and development partners, while work was ongoing on another 900 facilities. He also disclosed that 19,758 skilled birth attendants had been recruited across 22 states, alongside 4,747 community health workers in 10 states, while 78,054 frontline health workers had received training. item.title: Amaechi Accuses APC Of Dodging Policy Debate, Focusing On Opposition
item.description: The vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of concentrating on opposition figures rather than presenting its policies and plans to Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. Amaechi, a former governor of Rivers State and minister of transportation, said the ruling party was more interested in weakening the opposition than engaging Nigerians on critical national issues. He made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Tuesday. According to him, the APC’s campaign rallies have largely focused on attacking opposition figures, particularly him, rather than addressing issues affecting the country. “The party in power is trying to look for how to weaken the opposition; they are scared. Don’t you see their campaign? Tell me one state they have campaigned in that is not about Amaechi; it’s all Amaechi, Amaechi, Amaechi, Ebonyi, Rivers, Amaechi,” he said. ﻿ Policy Debate Amaechi contrasted the ruling party’s approach with the opposition’s campaign, saying his party had focused on issues such as the economy, social housing and security. “When we were campaigning, we were addressing issues. We addressed the issues of economy, social housing, security,” the ex-minister said. Tinubu speaking at a state reception held in his honour at the newly constructed Banquet Hall of ARISE Palm Resort in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, following the APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, on Friday, November 6, 2026. He further argued that the APC was using his name as a recurring subject at its campaign events instead of explaining what it intended to do if re-elected. “You know what I do every morning? I call my children, [and] I say, ‘You see, your father has achieved so much that he is now the issue in the political discourse of Nigeria.’ NDC is not calling my name because we are in opposition. Anywhere APC is going tomorrow, it’s Amaechi they will mention; they won’t mention what they will do,” he said. View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. The former governor also dismissed what he described as the ruling party’s assurances that things would improve in the future, arguing that Nigerians deserved concrete policy proposals rather than promises. “They are not interested; what they are interested in is, ‘don’t worry, things will be better in the future, just put us in power.’ It’s a referendum,” he added. Amaechi contested the ADC presidential primary ahead of the 2027 election but lost to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. He is currently Atiku’s running mate on the party’s ticket. Campaigns Crowd at Atiku Abubakar’s presidential campaign rally in Kebbi. Amaechi’s comments come amid intensified campaigns by the APC ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. item.title: Anthropic Targets Valuation Of Up To $1.4 Trillion
item.description: Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing Tuesday, putting the company’s total valuation at up to $1.4 trillion. The maker of AI agent Claude said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares of Class A common stock at a Wall Street debut price estimate of “between $70.00 and $78.00” per share, amounting to $64.3 billion. Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion in its IPO, which would have made it the largest IPO on record. The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last. And it comes as Wall Street is busy digesting the impact of the US midterm elections, in which Democrats won majority control of both chambers of Congress and are vowing to put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda. Anthropic has been aiming to hold its initial public offering the week of November 16. This photograph shows the logo of the US artificial intelligence safety and research company Anthropic displayed on a smartphone’s screen in Brussels on June 10, 2026. Photo by NICOLAS TUCAT / AFP On Monday, the company announced it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful AI models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, which it said can perform 30 percent faster than previous versions. Growth has been staggering at the company. Anthropic’s revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from just $1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed earlier this month. On Tuesday, the company said its annualized projection, known as the run-rate revenue, “was approximately $81 billion as of October 31, 2026, up $10 billion from September 30.” Estimates in recent months had forecast Anthropic’s valuation at up to a staggering $2 trillion, but the estimates have slipped along with a slide in AI stock prices on Wall Street. Several US media outlets, including The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times on Tuesday estimated the valuation of the company at between $1.3 trillion and $1.4 trillion. item.title: Escalating CNG Prices: FG Threatens Sanctions Against Marketers Exploiting Unsuspecting Nigerians
item.description: The Federal Government has threatened to sanction marketers exploiting unsuspecting Nigerians over escalating prices of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) across the country. Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, spoke on Tuesday in Kano during the inspection of some CNG mother station infrastructure ahead of the commissioning of the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano AKK Pipeline and opening of two CNG daughter stations capable of dispensing CNG to more than 2,500 vehicles and 50 trucks daily. Ekpo during the opening of two CNG daughter stations capable of dispensing CNG to more than 2,500 vehicles and 50 trucks daily in Kano, on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. He said that the days of those exploiting Nigerian’s by taking advantage of the federal government’s CNG programme to acquire kits, buy CNG, and still charge unsuspecting Nigerians the same as those using petrol will soon be over. According to him, the goal is to flood the country with more CNG stations to meet the current high demand and encourage even more Nigerians, especially commercial drivers, to convert their vehicles. The minister also urged those alleging that the process of obtaining funds for CNG infrastructure expansion from the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund was not transparent and almost impossible. He challenged them to back such claims with evidence, adding that those who have complied with all the requirements have accessed the funds. item.title: Why an Instagram Following Tracker Can Reveal More Than a Profile’s Follower Count
item.description: A popular Instagram account can attract thousands of followers, but that number rarely tells the whole story. For businesses, content creators, and people researching social media trends, another question can be just as interesting: which accounts does that person choose to follow? Someone may publicly promote fashion, technology, or entertainment while following creators in entirely different fields. A business account may begin following emerging influencers long before announcing a collaboration. A public figure may gradually change the types of accounts appearing on their Following list. These observations can provide useful context, particularly when viewed over time. An Instagram following tracker helps organize changes to the accounts a public Instagram profile follows. Rather than relying on a single snapshot, tools such as Snoopreport record detected follows and unfollows across reporting periods. The results can support social media research, although they cannot explain why someone followed an account or reveal information that Instagram keeps private. Why Follower Counts Don’t Tell the Whole Story Follower numbers are among Instagram’s most visible statistics. They influence how people assess popularity, reach, and sometimes commercial value. Yet having a large audience doesn’t necessarily mean an account has a clearly defined set of interests or strong connections within a particular industry. The Following list offers a different perspective. Consider a technology commentator who starts following several artificial intelligence researchers, software companies, and digital policy organizations. Those additions may suggest topics worth investigating. Similarly, a lifestyle influencer who follows numerous local restaurants might be exploring a new content category. Neither example proves a professional plan or future collaboration. Following someone can reflect curiosity, personal connections, or temporary interest. Still, when researchers compare several observations across time, they may discover changes worth examining further. The Difference Between Following and Followers Before using an Instagram following tracker, it’s important to distinguish two commonly confused terms. Followers are people who subscribe to an account’s updates. Following refers to the accounts that the profile has chosen to follow. For example, a creator may have 40,000 followers while following only 600 accounts. A following tracker focuses on changes within those 600 connections, not on identifying people who recently followed the creator. Instagram allows users to inspect the Following list of an accessible public profile. However, the list doesn’t provide a dependable chronological history of when each connection was added. The order in which accounts appear should not be treated as a reliable record of recent follows. To understand changes, the list needs to be observed across different periods. item.title: What an Instagram Likes Viewer Can Tell Us About the Content People Enjoy
item.description: People reveal different sides of themselves on Instagram. Their profiles may feature carefully selected photographs, polished videos, and short biographies, but their everyday interactions with content can tell another story. A person who rarely posts about travel may regularly like photographs of unfamiliar destinations. A creator known for fashion might engage with technology tutorials, food videos, or sports content. These interactions can suggest topics that attract someone’s attention, even when they don’t appear on the person’s own profile. An Instagram likes viewer can help organize detected likes from public accounts, making it easier to identify recurring content themes rather than examining isolated posts. However, likes are an imperfect signal. They may indicate enjoyment, curiosity, support, or simply a momentary reaction. Understanding their limitations is essential before drawing conclusions. Why Instagram Likes Are So Interesting A like is one of the simplest interactions on social media. It takes only a moment, but it can reflect many different motivations. Someone might like a photograph because they admire the subject, appreciate the photography, support a friend, or agree with a message. For content creators and marketers, likes also form part of the wider picture of audience engagement. A beauty influencer may notice that certain makeup tutorials attract more engagement than product announcements. A restaurant could discover that behind-the-scenes videos generate stronger reactions than ordinary menu photographs. These observations can guide content decisions, especially when combined with comments, shares, reach, and other performance metrics. But there is an important difference between analyzing engagement on your own posts and studying what a particular public account likes elsewhere. Instagram makes the first task relatively straightforward. The second is more complicated. Can You See What Someone Likes on Instagram? Instagram lets users inspect the likes associated with individual posts they can access. For example, if a public photograph has received likes, its visible engagement information may show which accounts interacted with it. What Instagram doesn’t provide is a single public page listing all the posts another person has liked. The platform removed its old Following Activity tab in 2019. That feature previously offered a window into some activities of accounts people followed. Today, users can still explore publicly visible interactions, but building a comprehensive history of another account’s likes is not a standard Instagram feature. This is why an Instagram likes viewer is different from simply opening a photograph and checking its engagement.
